gx_front_1#1.killer: gold particles caught per 1-m sample by a 2-cm hole in placer pay gravel (bankable assay statistics)
gx_front_1#1.why: A finger-thin hole catches about one gold flake per metre even in a rich Kolyma placer, against ~20 needed for a +/-50% assay, so it cannot give bankable grade, and exploration is only ~6% of delivered cost anyway.

EC:EB:g1_loop#2.killer: share of Laptev-launched floes that reach Fram Strait
EC:EB:g1_loop#2.why: Even with chosen launch points at most half of Laptev ice ever joined the Transpolar Drift (about a fifth survives today), and bags, two years of 14% money and a token pickup already cost as much as the rail freight they replace.

EC:EB:g2_evo2#1.killer: near-bed wave orbital velocity needed to stir 0.5-mm sand in a 1-m-deep pond
EC:EB:g2_evo2#1.why: Waves on a pond this small are too short to reach the floor: even a gale stirs it at ~2 cm/s, a quarter of what 0.5-mm sand needs and ~5% of what 20-mm stones need, so the sorting that would halve placer cost never starts.

g1_mech#3.killer: yearly release volume to float 1.4 Mt of concentrate 100 km down a 20-m creek at 0.8 m depth
g1_mech#3.why: The barges fall behind the crest, so the release must run for the whole voyage, and one small-creek snowmelt carries under a quarter of a Baimskaya-size year while a free creek route would trim only the 5% outbound share.

erp2_a#3.killer: charge per kg of grain needed for the claimed 41-cm drift at 300 kV/m over a 1.5-m fall
erp2_a#3.why: Measured charging of the feldspar and quartz waste gives about half the claimed drift, and even the idea's own saving is under 3% of delivered lithium carbonate cost.

gx_fl_1#2.killer: hoop strap tension at the base of a 60-m tailings thickener holding 6 m of slurry, safety factor 4
gx_fl_1#2.why: The "a sixth of burst" check compares pressure, but strap tension grows with tank radius, so a 60-m thickener wall needs about 4x the hoop strength ever demonstrated, and the shells reach at most a quarter of capex.

g1_core2#2.killer: barrel life at ~1.5 km/s with 100-500 kg rounds
g1_core2#2.why: A gun this fast wears out its barrel in about 65 rounds against ~12,800 a day needed for Baimskaya, and the launch energy alone costs more than the whole outbound logistics bill.

gx_ledg_1#2.killer: seam area gasified per well pair
gx_ledg_1#2.why: Underground gasification itself is proven, but a well pair sweeps about 0.2 ha rather than the 1.5 ha assumed, and at 10 kt/yr the station's crew, plant and 2-3 new well pairs a year cost more than the barge and winter-road chain they remove.

EC:EB:g2_imm#3.killer: winter electricity from freezing the leach liquor vs electrowinning demand, per kg Cu (2 g/L PLS frozen 96% to reach CuSO4 saturation; Nov–Mar air −31 °C; 5 K/10 K heat-exchanger approaches; 0.6 of Carnot)
EC:EB:g2_imm#3.why: Freezing covers only ~60% of the electrowinning power (100% only if the whole season averaged −40 °C), and SX plus diesel are too small a share of cost to pay for a plant that must freeze ~480 t of liquor per tonne of copper.

EC:EB:g1_genius#3.killer: ice that must leave the sand before the dry electrostatic roll vs the "free drying" of −30 °C air
EC:EB:g1_genius#3.why: Frozen ground is not dry ground: the pore ice stays on the grains, and removing it with −30 °C air would take ~1.2×10^5 m³ of air per tonne of sand, so the gold never reaches the roll as free grains.

EC:EB:g2_evo1#3.killer: winter sublimation flux from the gravel pad
EC:EB:g2_evo1#3.why: The measured sublimation is about 1/3 of what is needed, so the pad would have to be ~3.3 km²; snowfall (~0.4 mm/day, ~5× the sublimation) buries it anyway, and the extra handling makes each ounce dearer.

g1_core2#1.killer: rate at which ponded, darkened yedoma deepens by thaw
g1_core2#1.why: A 1.5 m channel would take ~24 years to form (while the banks retreat ~1.2 m/yr), and even a finished canal only shortens one leg of the delivery chain.

EC:EB:g2_evo1#2.killer: under-ice river discharge needed to carry a season's sand (100,000 m³ of 1 mm sand over 120 days at 1.5 m/s under the keel; Meyer-Peter–Müller bedload formula)
EC:EB:g2_evo1#2.why: Placer rivers carry about 1/20 of the winter flow needed (most freeze through, or overflow as aufeis when the keel chokes them), and even a working version saves only the washing, ~8% of the chain.

g1_core2#3.killer: average amount the film surface must stay below air temperature over the thaw season to keep the thaw inside a 2 m gravel pad (Stefan formula: at most 541 °C·day of surface thawing)
g1_core2#3.why: The film supplies only ~60% of the cooling needed in the Arctic (~25% in central Yakutia), cannot be laid on driven-over or dusty surfaces, and foundations are too small a share of delivered cost for the chain to change.

gx_front_2#2.killer: ammonia made per tonne of ore ground vs ammonia the leach consumes (sulphide sulphur ends up as ammonium sulphate; ore with 1% Ni + 1% Cu)
gx_front_2#2.why: Even at the lab-record efficiency the mill makes about 1/1,000 of the ammonia the leach consumes, and if it did make it all, the electrolytic hydrogen alone ($746/t) would cost about three times the inbound logistics it removes ($255/t).

g1_mech#2.killer: reduction in hauled tonnage that dry electrostatic sorting achieves at usable recovery
g1_mech#2.why: Dry charge sorting achieves about half the required tonnage cut at worse recovery than the dense-media and flotation plants already concentrating on site, so the hauled tonnage does not fall and delivered cost rises.

gx_front_1#3.killer: specific energy to loosen frozen ground
gx_front_1#3.why: Even for the weakest stone type and only the ice volume, burst-wave fatigue needs 13x the energy the whole dozer fleet now spends per m3, so battery rigs would cost about $5,200/oz in power alone.

g1_loop#2.killer: fraction of pods (Siberian-shelf ice) that reach Fram Strait
g1_loop#2.why: At most about 20% of shelf ice now survives to Fram Strait, but the pods need about 89% to break even, so each delivered tonne costs about $800 against $130 by sea.

gx_fl_1#4.killer: site electricity per t LCE (salt splitting plus flash heating)
gx_fl_1#4.why: The scheme swaps reagents for 3.6x the electricity today's energy budget buys at winter-road diesel power, so it would survive only on a grid at about 11 rub/kWh or less, which a winter-road site does not have.

gx_ledg_1#3.killer: lithium the alumina hydrate can carry within smelter spec
gx_ledg_1#3.why: Lithium co-precipitates with the hydrate as intended, but 45 kt/yr would then need a full-stream strip removing 97.6% of it from all of Achinsk's alumina hydrate, not a small new circuit (and RUSAL said in Aug 2026 it may close Pikalyovo).

gx_front_2#3.why: Even the weakest kidney stones need 6x the energy of a whole crushing plant per tonne, and at realistic kimberlite strengths the cost rises to about $75/ct.

gx_front_2#1.killer: surplus power needed to heat the full ore stream to 600 C
gx_front_2#1.why: Heating every tonne needs 3.3x the site's entire generation, and the 19% easier grinding (Minerals 2022 12(5):593) returns only 2% of the charge energy, so each kWh pays about 1.02 times, not twice.

gx_fl_1#3.killer: settlements with a coal deposit within about 100 km on their river
gx_fl_1#3.why: The economics are strong because the 85% logistics share collapses, but the idea works only where coal outcrops on the same river, at most about 40% of Arctic Yakutia's settlements, so it needs a field inventory of coal bluffs and water-protection-zone permits.

g1_genius#3.killer: gold recovery with dry separation of frozen gravel
g1_genius#3.why: Measured dry recovery falls short of break-even, and even at equal recovery year-round dry work saves only about 17%, because earthmoving and mineral extraction tax dominate the cost.

gx_front_2#4.killer: fraction of gold left in the calcine after a ~3,000 °C flash (Au boils at 2,856 °C; p_Au ≈ 1.7 atm; a 1-µm grain evaporates in ~17 µs)
gx_front_2#4.why: At 3,000 °C the gold boils off with the arsenic. Even if it stayed, the container only replaces a ~$250/oz link (POX capex $46/oz, POX opex ≤$122/oz, freight $81/oz), while its 939 kWh/t of flash power at 41 rub/kWh costs ~$223/oz (RATIO 1.09 even at NPP power prices).

gx_fl_2#5.killer: pump pressure per 15-km hose segment at the −57.8 °C record low (ESPO-type crude at 6.95 cSt @20 °C, extrapolated with the Siberian Light slope to 124 cSt; laminar flow; +100 m rise)
gx_fl_2#5.why: The strapped hose survives the hydraulics, but trucking is only $10 of an $82/bbl chain that is ~53% tax. The hose alone ($180/m aramid-TPU catalogue price, shop.midwesthose.com, $54M) amortises to $6.5/bbl, and even the claimed $1/bbl reaches only 1.12.

gx_ledg_2#2.killer: diesel per gram to hot-water thaw, jet and airlift the paystreak (20 vol% pore ice = 69 MJ/m³; 60% of heat reaches the ore; 85% boiler; grade 1.75 g/m³; 85% recovery)
gx_ledg_2#2.why: Ideal thaw alone already takes 1.5 l/g, so the 2 l/g claim fails. Each cased 0.3-m hole through 20 m of cover yields only ~2.7 oz and costs ≥$3,900 even at US double-cased rates (softlive.floridadep.gov). That adds ~$1,440/oz, more than the stripping fleet it removes.

gx_fl_2#4.killer: flash Joule heating (FJH) throughput for run-of-mine pegmatite (1.96 Mt/yr; 43.6 t ore per t LCE; 210 MW, or 140 MW after the thermophotovoltaic recapture)
gx_fl_2#4.why: The chemistry works in the lab, but the pit needs ~1,000x the largest FJH plant that exists. Heating all 43.6 t of ore per tonne also costs 27 MWh/t ($2,094/t at 6.45 rub/kWh), so even the claimed tenfold process-capex cut gives only ~1.2x.

gx_fl_2#1.killer: diesel to thaw the scoring slots (0.2-m back, side and base slots on 10×3×8.3 m slabs = 11% of volume; 30 vol% ice; 100% heat use) against one-tenth of today's dozer diesel
gx_fl_2#1.why: The <1 bar cushions can tip a slab (6x the restoring moment). But melting even the thinnest slots takes about as much diesel per m³ as ripping and dozing does now, ~7x the claimed one-tenth budget.

gx_ledg_2#5.killer: dredging depth to the pit floor (70 Mt/yr ore × ~25 yr × strip ratio 0.8 = 1.17 km³ → 230–390 m mean depth over 3–5 km²; ~47 m of deepening in year 1 on 1 km²; ore traced to 750 m)
gx_ledg_2#5.why: No dredge reaches below ~45 m, so the floating mine stalls within the first year or two of a pit that must go several hundred metres deep. Even the claimed capital halving, with no dredge or barge cost added, gives only 1.26x.

EC:EB:g1_core2#1.killer: water needed to hold barge depth in the gravity-graded channel after the lake drains (1.5 m × 15 m for ≤400-t Kolyma barges; n 0.03; slope 0.1 m/km → 8.7 m³/s over a 100-day season)
EC:EB:g1_core2#1.why: Lake heat could cut the gully: about 86,000 m³ of 12 °C water per km melts the 65–90 vol% yedoma ice (epic.awi.de/35773). But water draining to the river leaves no navigable canal behind, and the road leg it replaces is a few percent of delivered cost.

gx_ledg_1#5.killer: throughput per rope-conveyor line at 25 Mt/yr and 85% availability
gx_ledg_1#5.why: The comparison is with Elga's own railway at ~$12/t (built for ~100 bn rub, about $2.2M/km), not the $46/t RZD tariff. A 450-km elevated belt costs more per tonne: $3.2bn → $16.8/t (from bulk-online's $2.07M/km at 10 Mtpa, scaled), or $45/t at Thundersaid's average $0.1/t-km. It would also need ~3x the capacity and ~90x the length of any RopeCon built.
